about: Sixteen slides from four decks that passed every gate. Query with scripts/pick_exhibit.py; do not read this file whole.

palettes.broadside: ink and fire orange, no third hue (#d2521e on #1b1614)

exhibits.carries: One sentence of bad news, with the three numbers that size it
best_for: postmortem opening
incident review
a number the room must not forget
avoid_for: more than three figures
figures that need units explained
exhibits.watch: The figure and its label are one thought. Set the label under the number, never beside it, and never past twelve words.

exhibits.carries: A question or claim carried by type alone, with provenance in a thin meta strip
best_for: scientific or regulated openings
when any image would look decorative
a light deck that starts quiet
avoid_for: a title under eight words, which leaves the slide empty
openings that need to show a thing
exhibits.watch: A light hero lives or dies on the size jump. If the title is not at least three times the meta strip, the slide reads as a form.

exhibits.carries: The deck's subject rendered as a full-bleed drawing behind the title
best_for: physical systems
networks and infrastructure
a deck that needs one memorable image
avoid_for: abstract subjects with no honest picture
body slides, which must stay native
exhibits.watch: The drawing must say something. This one thins and breaks its lines left to right because that is the argument. Atmosphere with no claim in it is decoration.

exhibits.carries: One declaration at full volume on a saturated field, with the whole top of the frame left empty
best_for: an opening that has to land before the speaker talks
a single finding the rest of the deck answers
a section marker or a closing line
avoid_for: anything with a second idea in it
a headline over about eight words, which drops the type below display size
body slides, whose text must stay small enough to read as information
exhibits.watch: The void above the block is the composition. Centring the type, or filling the space with a subtitle and a logo, turns a poster back into a slide. Set a measure so the headline breaks into two lines; without one it runs the full width as a strip.

exhibits.carries: One sentence the room should hold, with nothing else in the frame
best_for: the pivot between two halves of a deck
a quoted line from a customer, a regulator, or the room itself
the sentence a speaker wants four seconds of silence after
avoid_for: a sentence that needs evidence on the same slide
more than about twenty-five words
a claim the deck has not yet earned
exhibits.watch: One accent phrase, not three. A statement slide that also carries a subtitle, an image, or a takeaway strip is a body slide wearing the wrong clothes.

exhibits.carries: A trend crossing a line that means something
best_for: a metric degrading past a limit
before and after a policy date
any claim of the form 'and then it crossed'
avoid_for: more than three series
categories that are not ordered
exhibits.watch: The threshold needs its own label inside the plot, not in a legend. A dashed line nobody can name is furniture.

exhibits.carries: A comparison across arms where the uncertainty is part of the claim
best_for: trial endpoints
A/B results
any comparison where a reader will ask 'is that difference real'
avoid_for: point estimates you cannot bound
more than six categories
exhibits.watch: Annotations at the right edge run out of viewBox before they run out of slide. Anchor them by measured width, and shorten the words before you shrink the type.

exhibits.carries: A count out of a population, shown as the population
best_for: '38 of 214' where the 214 matters
risk exposure
replacing a percentage nobody feels
avoid_for: populations over about 400 dots
two proportions compared, which wants bars
exhibits.watch: Size the matrix first, then give the text column what is left. Sizing the text first is how the grid track collapses and the copy runs off the slide.

exhibits.carries: How a population narrowed, stage by stage, with the losses named
best_for: CONSORT and funnel disposition
eligibility and attrition
a pipeline where the drop-off is the point
avoid_for: flows that branch and rejoin
processes with no quantities
exhibits.watch: Side branches are the interesting part and the part that overflows. Every label sits inside its own box or outside every box, never half.

exhibits.carries: A dated sequence where the gap between two events is the argument
best_for: how long something went undetected
decision history
a delay you are accountable for
avoid_for: more than about six events
durations you cannot date
exhibits.watch: Centred labels collide long before anything clips. Space events by label width, not by date, and shade the span you are arguing about.

exhibits.carries: An explanation that needs sentences, with one small exhibit holding the proportion
best_for: causal explanation
when the honest answer is a paragraph
the slide after a chart, saying why
avoid_for: anything a chart alone would carry
two exhibits, which makes it a dashboard
exhibits.watch: This is the form that saves a deck from being all charts. Keep the exhibit subordinate: if it is more than a third of the width it stops supporting the prose and starts competing with it.

exhibits.carries: A set of things checked, each with a verdict and a one-line reason
best_for: why none of the controls caught it
options considered and rejected
a checklist where the reasons differ
avoid_for: items with identical reasons, which is a bullet list
more than six rows
exhibits.watch: Rules between rows, not boxes around them. A wall of equal cards flattens exactly the difference between rows that this form exists to show.

exhibits.carries: Today against the proposal, item for item
best_for: a change of process
current versus target
a recommendation that needs its baseline visible
avoid_for: three or more options, which wants a table
comparisons where the items do not pair up
exhibits.watch: Both columns get the same rules and the same type. The moment the proposal column is prettier, the slide is selling instead of comparing.

exhibits.carries: Two positions, each given a whole ground, where the choice between them is the slide
best_for: a recommendation set against the submitted case
build versus buy, keep versus retire, now versus later
two options that need three reasons apiece, not a one-line contrast
avoid_for: three or more options, which the split cannot hold
item-for-item comparison, which is compare-two-states
options that differ only in degree
exhibits.watch: The surface colour is the argument, so neither half needs a card, a panel, or a border. Keep the two halves structurally identical and let only the content differ; a taller left column reads as the answer before anyone has read it.

exhibits.carries: Values the audience will read one by one, not a shape they will see
best_for: safety and adverse-event data
rate comparisons across arms
anything a reader will quote
avoid_for: a trend, which wants a line
fewer than about four rows
exhibits.watch: A real <table> converts natively and stays editable. Numbers right-aligned, one rule under the head, no vertical rules and no zebra fill.

exhibits.carries: What will be done, by whom, by when
best_for: the last slide of anything that asks for a decision
commitments after an incident
a plan the room must hold you to
avoid_for: actions with no named owner, which is not a commitment
more than four rows
exhibits.watch: A date with no name beside it is a wish. If you cannot fill the owner column the slide is not ready, and no styling fixes that.
